sources.quote: which becomes mandatory once taxable revenue passes $30,000 in a quarter or across four consecutive quarters
sources.title: When to register for and start charging the GST/HST - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: You are no longer a small supplier and you must register for the GST/HST if your total revenues from taxable supplies (and those of your associates) are over $30,000 ($50,000 for public service bodies) in a single calendar quarter or over the last four consecutive calendar quarters.

sources.quote: the grant covers eligible third-party training costs to roughly $10,000 per trainee, and employers under 100 staff pay at least one sixth in cash
sources.title: Ontario Job Grant | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: Employers with under 100 employees are required to pay at least one-sixth of the training costs of each trainee. The Ontario Job Grant supports eligible training costs up to a maximum of $10,000 per trainee, with additional flexibility for small employers.

sources.quote: Alberta having replaced its job grant with the Canada-Alberta Productivity Grant
sources.title: Canada-Alberta Productivity Grant | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: The Canada-Alberta Productivity Grant is an employer-driven program which replaces the Canada-Alberta Job Grant, and reimburses part of the training expenses to boost productivity and workforce competitiveness.

sources.quote: an employer whose total payroll exceeds $2 million must spend at least one percent of payroll on eligible training or remit the shortfall to Revenu Québec
sources.title: Contribution to the Workforce Skills Development and Recognition Fund | Revenu Québec
sources.evidence: If your total payroll for the year is over $2 million, you are required to participate in workforce skills development for the year by allotting an amount representing at least 1% of your total payroll to eligible training expenditures. The contribution to the Workforce Skills Development and Recognition Fund (WSDRF) must be remitted no later than the last day of February of the following year.

sources.quote: is reviewable unless it rests on an adequate and proper test conducted before the claim was made, and the burden of proof sits with the advertiser
sources.title: Performance claims not based on an adequate and proper test
sources.evidence: Under paragraph 74.01(1)(b) of the Competition Act, a person engages in reviewable conduct who makes a representation to the public in the form of a statement, warranty or guarantee of the performance, efficacy or length of life of a product that is not based on an adequate and proper test thereof, with the proof lying on the person making the representation. The test must have been done before the claim is made.

sources.quote: Since 20 June 2025 private parties can seek leave from the Competition Tribunal to bring these applications themselves
sources.title: Competition Bureau issues a revised bulletin on private access to the Competition Tribunal - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: On June 20, 2025, the Competition Bureau published a revised information bulletin on private access to the Competition Tribunal following changes to the Competition Act that came into force that date. These changes further expand private access to the Tribunal including by allowing applications related to deceptive marketing and by easing the legal test used to determine which applications can proceed.

sources.quote: only a lawyer, a Quebec notary or a member of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants may advise on an immigration application for a fee
sources.title: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act SC 2001, c 27 - Section 91
sources.evidence: Section 91(1): no person shall knowingly, directly or indirectly, represent or advise a person for consideration — or offer to do so — in connection with the submission of an expression of interest or a proceeding or application under this Act. Exceptions: a lawyer who is a member in good standing of a law society of a province or a notary who is a member in good standing of the Chambre des notaires du Québec; any other member in good standing of a law society of a province or the Chambre des notaires du Québec, including a paralegal; or a member in good standing of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants.

sources.quote: verify with your address, then hide it and define the regions you serve
sources.title: Manage your business address - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: If you don't serve customers at your business address, such as for a service-area business, you can choose to not show your address and list your service area instead. If you're a plumber and run your business from your residential address, clear the address from your Business Profile.
